info.title: tripo/v3.1-20260211-image-to-model
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "tripo/v3.1-20260211-image-to-model", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. `x-comfy-router-input-modalities` records the media kinds the model is documented to accept; the request schema is shared across sibling models and may admit media kinds this model ignores. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Request body for a Tripo image-to-3D generation on Comfy Router. `input` is required. Omit `model`: the model id selects the Tripo version and Router fills it.

input.description: A file token, a public URL, or an earlier task id.

model.description: Tripo model version. Omit it or send null when using Comfy Router; the version is selected by the model id (for example `v3.1-20260211` for `tripo/v3.1-20260211-image-to-model`). Omitting it is recommended. A supplied version must name the id's version in Tripo's own casing (for example `P2-20260801` for `tripo/p2-20260801-image-to-model`), not the lowercase spelling the id uses.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Tripo v3 generation models: the terminal `GET /proxy/tripo/v3/tasks/{task_id}` task document, forwarded unchanged. The operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — the submit answers with a `{"code": 0, "data": {"task_id": ...}}` handle and Router polls on the caller's behalf — so the body a caller receives is the finished task rather than that handle.
THE ASSET IS `data.output.model_url`, the generated mesh. Comfy Router answers a `success` task with no `model_url` as a Comfy Router error rather than with this document, so a `200` here always carries one. `data.output.rendered_image_url` is a preview render, not the asset. The URLs are Tripo's own links: Router does not re-host them onto Comfy storage, so download the asset rather than storing the link.
`data.status` is Tripo's own vocabulary. `success` is the one terminal success and the only value this document carries: `failed`, `banned`, `expired` and `cancelled` reach a Router caller as a Comfy Router error rather than as this body, as does a task still `queued` or `running` when Router stops polling.
`data.type` follows the operation: `text_to_model`, `image_to_model` or `multiview_to_model` for the text, image and multiview ids. The example shows a text-to-model task.

credits_consumed.description: Actual credits consumed by the task. Present once status is finalized; 0 for failed tasks.

status.description: One of: queued, running, success, failed, cancelled.
